Subject: Evidence export constraints / SIEM integration questions

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the demo last week. We are starting procurement/internal-risk review for the Private deployment and the security team has a handful of concrete constraints they want to validate with you before we move to an architecture review: 

- No outbound UDP allowed from the enclave; only HTTPS/TCP egress to approved endpoints.
- All exported logs/metrics must land in our Splunk HEC instance behind a NAT with mutual TLS.
- PII fields must be redacted or pseudonymized at source; we prefer tokenization using our KMS.
- Retention: 90 days of full raw logs, 1 year of indexed metadata.
- Audit trail: evidence manifests for every daily export (signed).

I attached the security questionnaire with a few SIEM-specific items (nimbus_siem_questions.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood's recommended forwarder for Private deployments can meet the above constraints and how we should structure the network egress?

We'd like to schedule a technical deep-dive next week (30–45m) with your infra/security engineer and our SOC lead. Proposed time slots attached.

Appreciate it — Alex

--

Sr. InfoSec Engineer | Nimbus Financial

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up front: yes — the Private deployment pattern we propose supports HTTPS/TCP-only egress, mutual TLS to customer HEC, local redaction hooks, and signed daily manifests. Below I've sketched the recommended architecture and an initial mapping to each of your constraints.

----- Original message from Alex Soto 
On Fri, 1 Jun 2028 at 09:12 -0700, Alex Soto <alex.soto@nimbus.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the demo last week...

Recommended architecture (high level):
- Customer-side forwarder (containerized OpenTelemetry + Redwood forwarder shim) runs inside customer VPC / enclave.
- Forwarder -> local OTEL collector -> Redwood forwarder shim -> outbound connection to Redwood Evidence Proxy (ep.rw-infra.com) over mutual TLS (mTLS).
- Redwood Evidence Proxy terminates mTLS, validates client cert, and forwards to a customer-configured Splunk HEC endpoint over an outbound, authenticated channel (HEC token + mTLS if you require).
- For on-prem: option to keep the Evidence Proxy as a deployed VM/HA pair in your DMZ if policy disallows outbound to public endpoints.

Mapping to your constraints:
- No UDP: forwarder and HEC path use TLS/TCP only. We don't require UDP.
- Mutual TLS: supported end-to-end; we can supply client certs per deployment or accept customer-signed certs.
- PII redaction: forwarder includes a configurable redact/pseudonymize filter plugin. For strict KMS tokenization, we can call your KMS via a restricted egress interface or run a local tokenization sidecar.
- Retention: Redwood retains only transient state in private deployments unless explicitly configured; we will deliver daily signed manifests and you control downstream retention at your HEC.
- Audit manifests: each day the forwarder will emit a signed manifest (SHA256) listing batches sent; manifest signing uses deployment-level key material (can be stored in your HSM).

Attachments: redwood_private_evidence_playbook_v1.pdf (design + checklist), and I've attached an answer matrix in the Drive link for the SOC.

Next steps / asks:
1) Can you confirm whether Nimbus prefers Redwood-supplied client certs or will provide certs (we need to know for provisioning)?
2) Please confirm expected Splunk HEC URL and whether you require HEC tokens + mTLS.
3) Let's lock a 45-minute technical call next Tue/Thu.

I'll loop in Kimberly for KMS/key questions and Ben for the forwarder runtime hardening checklist.

Thanks,
Jordan

Jordan / Ben / Alex — adding details from the infra/security side. Quoting Jordan's summary above for context.

Key operational controls we recommend for Nimbus (and questions where we need your preference):

1) Certificate provisioning: we support two patterns — (A) Redwood issues per-deployment client certs signed by our internal CA and we deliver the certificate bundle via the Private control plane, or (B) Nimbus supplies certs signed by your PKI and we validate the chain. Option B is preferable when your policy requires customer-controlled cert lifecycle. Please indicate preference.

2) KMS integration / tokenization: if you elect to tokenise at source using your KMS, the forwarder will need outbound HTTPS to your KMS endpoint. If that outbound is disallowed, we can run a lightweight tokenization sidecar inside the enclave that holds a short-lived key from your HSM. We will provide a KMS key-rotation matrix (attached: kms_key_rotation_matrix.xlsx) and recommended rotation cadence.

3) Network ACLs / egress filtering: open only to the evidence proxy FQDN/IP range and your HEC endpoint; we support pinned IP ranges and short-lived SRV records if you require ephemeral IPs.

4) Tracing hooks: for trace correlation we recommend OTLP over gRPC to a local collector; traces and logs should carry the same request_id header. Sampling rate should be agreed: we suggest 1% baseline with on-demand ramp to 10% for incidents. 

5) Hardening: container images are signed (cosign) and we publish SBOMs for the forwarder. We also run a minimal, non-root runtime and restrict capabilities.

Action items before the technical call:
- Nimbus: confirm certing pattern and HEC URL + token requirements.
- Redwood: prepare per-deployment network IP ranges, a sample manifest format, and a draft runbook for daily manifest verification.

Alex — does the proposed tokenization sidecar approach sound feasible if your environment restricts outbound KMS calls?

Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park

Jordan / Kimberly — thanks, this is the level of detail we needed. Short answers: 

- Certs: Nimbus will supply certs from our enterprise PKI (Option B).
- HEC: We'll provide the HEC URL and HEC token via the secure procurement CTA; HEC will accept mTLS + token.
- KMS: outbound HTTPS to our KMS is allowed but only to a short list of FQDNs; we'll share those on the call.
- Manifests: yes, manifests need to be SHA256 + timestamped + signed by a key we trust (we'll assess whether to accept Redwood-signed manifests or insist on customer-signed manifests).
